{"result":"# The Rust Programming Language and Memory Safety

Rust is a general-purpose language that balances performance, type safety, and concurrency [1]. Its multi-paradigm design draws on functional programming ideas [1].

Graydon Hoare began developing Rust in 2006, and Mozilla Research sponsored it from 2009 [2]. It had its first public release in 2010, and version 1.0 arrived in 2015 [2].

Memory safety protects programs from bugs such as buffer overflows and dangling pointers [3]. Java checks bounds at runtime [3]. C, C++, and Fortran allow unchecked pointer arithmetic [3].

Rust has C++-like syntax yet guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector [2]. Rather than classes and inheritance, it relies on structs, enums, and traits [1].

Rust therefore suits performance-critical systems programming, where memory safety matters and low-level control is still required. Its design aims to deliver both at once.
